concept: Balancer windows and per-collection balancing control
summary: Source-anchored research for Balancer windows and per-collection balancing control. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Read config.collections for the collection namespace and inspect noBalance: true means balancing is disabled; false or an absent field means it is enabled. A missing namespace must not be interpreted as an enabled collection. (high confidence)

A balancing window must be sufficient to complete migration of the data the deployment needs to redistribute, and the window should be chosen to support the deployment's needs. Leaving the balancer disabled for extended periods can lead to unbalanced shards and degrade cluster performance. Balancing can be disabled for a specific collection to support maintenance or atypical workloads such as data ingestions or exports, and re-enabled with sh.enableBalancing(). Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-sharded-cluster-balancer.md

Operational inference: range migrations carry bandwidth and workload overhead that can affect performance, and limiting the balancing window can keep that overhead away from production traffic, so scheduling automatic balancing outside a long-read interval can reduce overlap. This is not evidence that every long secondary read will complete: since MongoDB 8.2, long-running secondary reads may be automatically terminated before orphaned document deletion following a chunk migration. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration.md

MongoDB supports weekday-specific balancing windows through activeWindowDOW. When both activeWindow and activeWindowDOW are set, the balancer is active only for the windows configured with activeWindowDOW and ignores activeWindow. The MongoDB 8.3 compatibility notes say that on downgrade from 8.3 the day-of-week setting (named activeBalancerWindowDOW there) is not available, the balancer defaults to activeWindow, and custom day-of-week configurations made in 8.3 do not apply. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-sharded-cluster-balancer.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/8.3-compatibility.md

In MongoDB 7.0 and later, AutoMerger participates in balancing operations; when a balancing window is configured it runs only within that window. Collection-level AutoMerger controls provide a separate way to disable automatic merges. (high confidence)

Configure a daily cluster-wide balancing window by updating the config.settings document with _id "balancer" and activeWindow containing start and stop values in HH:MM format. The balancer must also be enabled; setting a window does not override its stopped state. (high confidence)

Use sh.disableBalancing("database.collection") and sh.enableBalancing("database.collection") through mongos to control one collection. Disabling that collection leaves other collections eligible for automatic balancing. (high confidence)

Check collection state through config.collections for the namespace: noBalance: true means balancing is disabled. Separately distinguish cluster permission to run, reported by sh.getBalancerState(), from current activity, reported by sh.isBalancerRunning(); an enabled balancer can be idle. (low confidence)

SERVER-72820 documents a test-helper failure mode: awaitCollectionBalance changed collection balancing through config.collections writes that needed retry handling for notPrimary errors during config-server stepdown. The issue records a fix version of 7.0.0-rc0; it does not establish a current production bug. (low confidence)

sh.getBalancerState() indicates whether the balancer is enabled (true) or disabled (false), rather than whether data is currently migrating. Check the current state of the balancer separately with sh.isBalancerRunning(), which in mongosh returns a document including mode and inBalancerRound. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/sh.getBalancerState.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/sh.isBalancerRunning.md

The current manual describes activeWindowDOW as an array of named-day windows, including multiple windows per day, and says it takes precedence over activeWindow. SERVER-82487 records the day-of-week feature with fix version 8.3.0-rc0; treat this as version-specific rather than an option available on all older releases. (high confidence) (verified as of 2025-12-22) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-sharded-cluster-balancer.md ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-82487

For a selected collection, run sh.disableBalancing('database.collection') through mongos before its maintenance or atypical workload, and sh.enableBalancing('database.collection') afterward. Disabling does not interrupt in-progress migrations; enabling permits future balancing rather than immediately forcing redistribution. (low confidence)

Disabling balancing on a collection does not interrupt migrations already in progress. Enabling balancing again does not immediately redistribute data; the collection becomes eligible for later balancing activity. (low confidence)

Time-zone assumptions are deployment-specific: the MongoDB manual evaluates self-managed windows in the config-server primary's time zone and Atlas windows in UTC, whereas Alibaba documents ApsaraDB window times in the instance region's local time zone. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-sharded-cluster-balancer.md ; https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/use-cases/manage-the-apsaradb-for-mongodb-balancer

The balancing window must be long enough to handle the deployment's accumulated balancing work. A very short window or prolonged disabling can leave shards unbalanced and degrade cluster performance. (high confidence)

Upstream MongoDB documents sh.stopBalancer() as allowing an in-progress migration to finish before stopping. Therefore a pause request is not evidence of instantaneous migration quiescence; verify activity before beginning a protected workload. (low confidence)
